title: What can you say about vitamin B12 in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 5 wordings for vitamin B12; the strongest is "Plays a part in normal energy metabolism" (strong, 0.14-1,000 µg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats anemia, including pernicious anemia".

supported_wordings.wording: Plays a part in normal energy metabolism.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists energy metabolism and the EU authorizes normal energy-yielding metabolism.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 0.14-1,000 µg a day for adults 19 and older. EU: at least 0.375 µg, 15% of the 2.5 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS: no upper limit was set.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Boosts energy for people with chronic fatigue
wordings_to_avoid.why: Implies an effect on a medical condition; the supported wording is normal energy metabolism and less tiredness.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
